question: In Table 1D-1, what standard abbreviations are permitted for 'Pedestrian(s)'?
model_answer: Direct Answer: Table 1D-1 lists two acceptable standard abbreviations for "Pedestrian(s)": **PED** and **PEDS**. When the word needs to be abbreviated on a traffic control device, one of these abbreviations must be used, and the same abbreviation should be used consistently throughout a single jurisdiction. Standards (mandatory): - "When the word messages shown in Table 1D-1 need to be abbreviated in connection with traffic control devices, the abbreviations shown in Table 1D-1 shall be used." For Pedestrian(s), the table lists "PED, PEDS." Guidance (recommended): - "If Table 1D-1 or 1D-2 indicates that more than one abbreviation is allowed for a given word or phrase, the same abbreviation should be used throughout a single jurisdiction." Since both PED and PEDS are allowed, a jurisdiction should pick one and use it consistently. Visual evidence: [Image 1] shows the Table 1D-1 row "Pedestrian(s) — PED, PEDS" in the General Abbreviations list, with no asterisk restriction attached. [Image 5] shows the same table in its full page context (page 35), confirming the entry appears under Table 1D-1, Acceptable Abbreviations. Citations: - Section 1D.08 Standard §1 (p.34) - Section 1D.08 Guidance §5 (p.34) - Table 1D-1 (p.35)
